The test image is a microscopic view (100 µm scale bar) showing round/spherical structures clustered in grape-like masses on branching conidiophores/hyphae. This is a fungal microscopy image.

Key features:
- Spherical, translucent spores clustered in dense masses
- Branching supporting structures (hyphae/conidiophores)
- Scale ~100 µm

This pattern strongly resembles Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold) conidia, or possibly Rhizopus sporangiospores. Let me view one Gray Mold reference to confirm.

The reference image shows a macro stem lesion (not microscopic). The test image is a microscopy view.

Based on the microscopic morphology in the test image:
- Round, smooth, translucent conidia clustered in dense grape-like masses
- Branching conidiophores supporting the spore clusters
- Scale ~100 µm — matches Botrytis cinerea conidia size

This is the classic microscopic appearance of **Botrytis cinerea** (Gray Mold). The grape-like clustering of spherical conidia on branching conidiophores is the hallmark of this pathogen, and is exactly what produces the "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass" described in the symptom description.
